verses.text: Later, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. He said, "I am going to my wife's room." But her father would not let him go in.
"I was sure you hated her," he said, "so I gave her to your friend. Is not her younger sister more beautiful? Please take her instead."
Samson said to them, "This time I will not be to blame when I do harm to the Philistines."
So he went out and caught three hundred foxes. He tied them tail to tail in pairs and fastened a torch to every pair of tails.
He lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the Philistines' standing grain. He burned up the stacks of cut grain and the standing grain, and the olive groves too.

When the Philistines asked, "Who did this?" they were told, "Samson, the son-in-law of the man from Timnah, because his wife was given to his friend." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
Samson said to them, "Since you acted like this, I will not stop until I get my revenge on you."
He attacked them without mercy and killed many of them. Then he went down and stayed in a cave in the rock of Etam.
The Philistines went up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi.
The people of Judah asked, "Why have you come to fight us?" They answered, "We have come to tie up Samson and do to him what he did to us."

Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?" He answered, "I only did to them what they did to me."
They said to him, "We have come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said, "Promise me that you will not kill me yourselves."
"We agree," they answered. "We will only tie you up and hand you over to them. We will not kill you." So they tied him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
As he came near Lehi, the Philistines came toward him shouting. Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully on him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and they fell off his hands.
He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, grabbed it, and killed a thousand men with it.
Then Samson said, "With a donkey's jawbone I have made donkeys of them, piles on piles. With a donkey's jawbone I have killed a thousand men."
When he finished speaking, he threw away the jawbone. And the place was called Ramath Lehi, which means Jawbone Hill.
Because he was very thirsty, he cried out to the LORD, "You have given your servant this great victory. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?"

Then God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength came back and he felt alive again. So the spring was called En Hakkore, which means Caller's Spring. It is still there in Lehi.
Samson led Israel as judge for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
